checkpoint_h_conclusion: RBD supports fading state memory, but increased recurrent length and heterogeneous delays did not generally extend activity-expressed memory under the preregistered regime.

factorial_interpretation.alpha_length: no positive length effect detected by preregistered identity-decoding assay
factorial_interpretation.alpha_heterogeneity: observed +0.052 is entirely from short+heterogeneous cell; not a general heterogeneity effect
factorial_interpretation.alpha_interaction: cancels short-hetero signal in long-hetero cell
factorial_interpretation.bootstrap_cis: not computed; +0.052 is prospective point estimate only, not statistically established

exploratory_note.status: exploratory only; not a revised confirmation; candidate for future independently preregistered protocol

recurrence_diagnostic.interpretation: no detected recurrence peaks under H4 frozen detector and Delta_max
recurrence_diagnostic.note: extending Delta_max would be H5/new protocol, not H4 correction

methodological_limitations: Cross-N identity decoding confounded by different class counts (P_chance=1/3 vs 1/12), sample complexity, and feature dimensionality
Do not conclude 'length has no effect on memory'; only that no positive length effect was detected by the preregistered H4 assay
Future topology-specific protocols may use matched binary perturbation decoding or information-normalized metrics

doctrine_updates.deprecated_claim: long heterogeneous networks maintain memory much longer
doctrine_updates.replacement_claim: recurrent geometry and delays determine how RBS perturbations are distributed in time and space, but increased path length or delay heterogeneity does not by itself guarantee increased decodable memory
